:::{#rem-overfitting-tradeoff}
#### Overfitting and the trade-off

By @thm-epe-decomposition,
$\epe{x}$ is the squared bias plus the variance plus $\sigma^2$.
Under a [bias--variance trade-off](#def-bias-variance-tradeoff)
among $g_1, \ldots, g_L$,
moving from $g_l$ to $g_{l+1}$
lowers $\epe{x}$ when the squared bias falls by more than the variance rises,
and raises it otherwise.
The smallest $\epe{x}$ is often at some $g_l$ with $1 < l < L$
[@james2021islr2e, sec. 2.2.2],
but not always:
if the mean function $\mean$ is a candidate of $g_1$,
the squared bias of $g_1$ can be zero,
and then no later $g_l$ has a smaller squared bias
and, under the trade-off, none has a smaller variance,
so none has a smaller $\epe{x}$.
[Overfitting](#def-overfitting) is what happens past the smallest error:
a procedure there has lowered its squared bias
by less than it has raised its variance.

:::
